title: Choose the booking composition
question: All three use the Courtline Scheduler identity. Choose the layout that should become the React interface.

options.label: Weekly Court
options.thesis: The entire week becomes one playable court, with the next available slot always visible.
options.viewport: Sport tabs and the week rail sit above a large court-line schedule; the booking summary stays fixed at the right.
options.risk: The full grid carries more information than some phone users need at once.

options.label: Daily Scoreboard
options.lineage: referee score sheet and game-day fixture board
options.thesis: One day takes center court, making the shortest path to an available slot unmistakable.
options.viewport: A large date scoreboard leads into three facility lanes; selecting a time opens a horizontal booking strip along the bottom.
options.risk: Comparing multiple days requires one more interaction than the weekly view.

options.label: Facility Lanes
options.lineage: recreation-center lane board and court assignment sheet
options.thesis: Facilities become clear lanes while dates and times remain lightweight controls above them.
options.viewport: A narrow filter bench leads into facility columns with bold open-slot blocks and a compact booking pass layered at the lower right.
options.risk: The lane layout is efficient but less dramatic than the full-court composition.
